world_sweep.oil_supply_demand: Counterweight: OPEC+ raising production into a 2026 glut; IEA and OPEC both cut 2026 demand by ~1.6 mb/d because of the closure. JPM sees Brent $86 Q3 -> $80 Q4 -> $78 year end. Goldman also lower.
world_sweep.uranium: Long-term contract uranium $90/lb, highest since 2008. 2025 supply 173M lb vs demand 204M lb. AI datacenters: DOE projects 12% of US electricity by 2028; Constellation guides hyperscaler spend +75% YoY. Strongest structural signal found — but untradeable, see blocked_ideas.
world_sweep.semis: Nvidia China AI-chip share forecast to fall 40% -> 8%; Huawei Ascend 950 rated comparable to H200; export policy incoherent with a 25% tariff. Structurally negative for NVDAX.
world_sweep.crypto: 08-19 rally on SEC proposed framework (mature assets exiting securities classification) plus Treasury doubling bond buybacks — amplified by ~$1.44B of short liquidations.
world_sweep.fed: Held 3.50-3.75% but 9-3 with three dissenters wanting a hike; September hike odds ~72%. FOMC minutes 2026-08-20 18:00 UTC.

orders.reasoning: Most direct tradeable expression of the largest live geopolitical event. Hormuz is under active naval blockade with no negotiations, yet USOX is calm at +2.11% and oil sits ~$86 — well below the $105 it printed on 23 July. The market is pricing reopening and the OPEC+ glut. That makes the payoff asymmetric: escalation or simple persistence retests ~$105 (+22%), resolution takes oil to ~$78 (-9%). Book is liquid (0.03% spread, deep top of book) so entry cost is negligible.
orders.counter_case: The closure is simultaneously bearish demand — the same blockade is why IEA/OPEC cut forecasts 1.6 mb/d. Both Goldman and JPM forecast oil lower into year end, and OPEC+ keeps adding barrels. If Hormuz reopens this is a fast -10%. USOX also tracks WTI futures, so contango decay bleeds a long position held for months.
orders.falsifier: A credible US-Iran negotiation restart, or confirmed reopening of Hormuz transit. Also exit if WTI closes below ~$80, which would confirm glut over geopolitics.

orders.reasoning: Pass 1 found the USOX thesis strengthened, not merely intact: all three falsifiers moved further away. Trump cut off talks and announced secondary sanctions on any country supporting Iran (a genuine supply removal, ~1.5 mb/d of Iranian exports, distinct from the Hormuz transit story); Iran put ballistic missiles into UAE territory and the UAE severed all trade and financial ties. WTI printed 87.16, a four-week high. On the priced-in scan USOX is the LEAST moved of everything that moved (+2.93% vs silver +4.27% and crypto +10-20%), while being the most direct instrument of the largest live event, and WTI at 87 still sits well below the 105 it printed on 23 July. Everything else on the menu was either already traded out (crypto, on forced short covering) or not expressible long-only (short equities/NVDAX).
orders.counter_case: Five arguments against, all still standing. (1) Concentration: this takes USOX to ~50% of a 150 USDT book. (2) EIA sees Brent averaging 69/b in 2027 as inventories rebuild and OPEC+ keeps adding barrels — the glut is real and this is a timing trade, not a structural one. (3) Trump escalate-then-deal is a well-worn pattern and CNN openly questions whether he stays the course; a surprise deal is a fast -10%. (4) +3.3% of today is already traded. (5) USOX tracks WTI futures and bleeds on contango. Sixth and heaviest: there is NO resting downside protection possible on this venue and I do not exist between runs. That last point gated the trade — I planned to skip the add if a stop could not be rested, then revised on learning WHY it could not: the spot API has no stop type at all, and this is unleveraged spot, which cannot be liquidated. Bounded drawdown, not ruin. So it moderated the size (25, not the 40-50 the conviction would otherwise justify) rather than vetoing it. Half the book stays in cash.
orders.falsifier: Unchanged and explicit: a credible restart of US-Iran negotiations, confirmed reopening of Hormuz transit, or WTI closing below 80. Add to those: visible follow-through failure on the secondary-sanctions threat (major buyers of Iranian crude carrying on unpunished within ~2 weeks).

orders.reasoning: The only resting order type this venue offers is a plain limit, so it is used where it actually helps. 148 is roughly WTI 95, a reachable escalation target (+9.2% from here). It covers ~35% of the position. Because I run only a few times a day, an intraday headline spike would otherwise be slept through and mean-revert before the next run; this converts the gap between runs from pure liability into partial asset on the upside. The remaining ~65% stays uncapped for the 105-retest case.
orders.counter_case: It caps 35% of the upside if oil runs straight through 148, and the units are frozen — a thesis-break exit next run requires cancelling this order first before selling. Both accepted as cheap.
orders.note: A protective stop below market is NOT possible here (see venue_findings). Handed to Erik as manual app steps instead.

orders.reasoning: Thesis DAMAGED, not broken - cut 50% of book to 25%. Falsifier 2 ('confirmed reopening of Hormuz transit') moved from abstract to concrete: Iran and Oman have agreed the coordinates of new shipping routes through the strait, Araghchi calls the deal 'very close', and the US/Iran/Oman are reported 'edging closer to an interim agreement that could reopen' it. The original thesis sentence was 'escalating, NOT resolving' - the second half now has a named counterparty and a mechanism. Three supporting marks: (a) the tape disagrees - on the most escalatory news day yet USOX is +1.31% while silver is +6.4%, gold +4%, ETH +17%, so oil is no longer leading its own story; (b) wrong benchmark - a Hormuz thesis is a Brent thesis and USOX tracks WTI, the least Hormuz-exposed crude (Brent 91.39 vs WTI 86.17 on the Pionex index); (c) contango bleed on a USO-style front-month roll. Reduce rather than close because the escalation leg is real and unfinished: Trump's 08-19 secondary-sanctions programme has not hit physical flows yet, only 8 vessels/day transit vs ~130 prewar, SPR is below 300M bbl for the first time since the early 1980s, and WTI at 86 is well above the $80 falsifier.
orders.counter_case: Trump's 'Economic D-Day' secondary sanctions were announced 08-19 and are the freshest, least-traded leg of the whole story - selling into them may be selling the day before they bite. If the sanctions remove ~1.5 mb/d of Iranian exports while Hormuz stays shut, WTI retests 105 and this trim costs the run. Accepted because the position stays open at 25%, so the upside is reduced rather than forfeited, and because a 50% single-name weight in a binary headline trade is indefensible on a book I cannot defend between runs.
orders.falsifier: If Hormuz transit normalises toward prewar volumes, or WTI closes below 80, close the remaining 0.2737 units. If instead secondary sanctions visibly bite and Brent takes out 100, the trim was wrong and the remainder should be re-added.

orders.reasoning: FISCAL DOMINANCE, not the war, is the event the world is trading. US public debt crossed $40 TRILLION for the first time. The 30-year yield hit 5.31% on Monday, the highest since 2007. The Treasury responded by DOUBLING its long-bond buyback operations from $2bn to a minimum of $4bn per operation, beginning 9 September; the 30y fell to 5.19% and the 10y to 4.66% on the announcement. The Treasury is now the marginal buyer of its own long end - that is the regime in which hard assets re-rate structurally. PRICED-IN CHECK, and it is what decides the trade: one day of the move is traded (gold +4%, silver +6.4% on 08-19), but the buyback operations DO NOT BEGIN UNTIL 9 SEPTEMBER. The catalyst has been announced, not executed; the flow is entirely ahead. INSTRUMENT CHOICE: PAXG is physically-backed gold with genuine 24/7 price discovery and no equity-issuer layer, which matters disproportionately for an agent that does not exist between runs and cannot rest a stop on this venue. It is also 8x more liquid than XAUT on Pionex (1.88M vs 232k 24h volume) and issued by a NYDFS-regulated trust. Entry was mid-range (4498.93 close, 4443.02-4517.05 range), unlike SLVX which was printing at its high.
orders.counter_case: Fed funds futures price roughly an 82% chance of a HIKE at the 16 September meeting, up from ~53% a week earlier, driven by exactly the oil shock this book is also long. A hike raises the carrying cost of a non-yielding metal and is the single strongest argument against this trade. Taking the other side deliberately: those odds rose to 82% over the same week silver rose ~8% and gold 4% - the market is already pricing the split, front end hikes while the long end gets monetised, and fiscal dominance is precisely the regime where metals rise THROUGH hikes. Secondary objections: buying after a vertical two-day move invites an ordinary 5% giveback, and gold plus oil are correlated inflation-impulse trades, though they run on different drivers (fiscal vs supply-geopolitics).
orders.falsifier: 1) The Treasury cancels, shrinks, or quietly under-executes the September 9 buyback programme. 2) The 30y yield falls back below ~4.75% on genuine demand rather than official support - the fiscal-stress premise dissolves. 3) Gold closes below ~4,250, breaking the trend that the buyback announcement started. 4) A September hike lands AND gold sells off with it, which would mean the front end is winning and my regime read is wrong.

orders.reasoning: Same fiscal-dominance thesis as PAXG, taken in the higher-torque instrument. Silver adds an independent supply leg: the Silver Institute has 2026 as the SIXTH consecutive annual supply deficit, with coin-and-bar demand +18% and US retail demand rebounding ~57%. DELIBERATE REVERSAL of run 2, and the reversal test was applied explicitly: run 2 rejected SLVX on the chain 'energy shock -> inflation -> Fed hikes -> silver damaged'. Since then hike odds went UP to 82% and silver went UP ~8%. The premise was falsified by events, not by discomfort at having missed a move - which is what makes reversing correct rather than a chase.
orders.counter_case: Three real objections. (1) The 82% September hike odds, as with PAXG. (2) SLVX is a tokenized ETF, not physical metal - it carries xStocks/Ondo issuer risk stacked on top of Pionex counterparty risk, and it references a market that is CLOSED off-hours while the token keeps trading, so it can gap at the US open. This is why it got the smaller slice. (3) Entry quality was poor: SLVX closed at 61.51, the exact high of its 24h range (low 59.18), and the fill came 61.98, above that. Buying strength off-hours in a thin token is the worst mechanical setup on the menu. Sized at 17% of book for exactly these reasons rather than matching the conviction of the idea.
orders.falsifier: 1) Same Treasury-programme falsifiers as PAXG. 2) The gold/silver ratio widens through ~75, meaning silver is losing the relative-value case. 3) Silver closes below ~62 spot (roughly SLVX 56), giving back the entire buyback-driven move. 4) The Silver Institute or a comparable primary source revises 2026 to a surplus.

Sound: (a) nothing else cleared the bar this run - crypto was already traded, LNGX was stale, defence was unresearched, shorts were rejected on structure; (b) a Hormuz reopening headline would hit USOX and soften the inflation impulse behind metals at the same time, so the book's downside is correlated. NOT SOUND, and this is the part that changed: holding 35% of the book in USDT while the central thesis of the book is that the US is monetising its own long end is a position AGAINST my own thesis. The 'keep ammunition' argument that justified it in the plan is also weak here: PAXG turns over 1.88M USDT a day and this is unleveraged spot, so any position is one market order from being cash again. Optionality you can buy back for a few basis points is not worth paying 35% of the book to hold. Deployed into PAXG rather than anything else because it is the highest-confidence idea on the sheet with its catalyst still entirely ahead (Treasury buybacks begin 9 September), it prices 24/7, it is physically backed with no equity-issuer layer, and it cannot be liquidated.
orders.counter_case: This raises metals to 60% of the book and hard-assets-plus-energy to 85%, which is genuine concentration in a single macro view. If the September FOMC hikes and gold sells off with it, both metal legs lose together and USOX gains nothing from it. Accepted because every leg is unleveraged spot with bounded drawdown and no liquidation risk, and because the alternative - sitting in the asset being debased - is not actually the safer choice under this thesis. Also a genuine entry cost: the add filled at 4520.02 versus 4507.32 for the first tranche, so averaging up by 0.3% after a +4% day. Retained 22.07 USDT (14.8%), which is a functional floor - two Pionex minimum orders - so the next run can act without a forced sale, not a nervous reserve.
orders.falsifier: Same as the PAXG opening order - Treasury under-executing or cancelling the 9 September programme, the 30y falling below ~4.75% on genuine demand, gold closing below ~4,250, or a September hike landing and gold selling off with it.

venue_findings.no_stop_orders: CONFIRMED by probe. Pionex spot API accepts MARKET and LIMIT only. STOP, STOP_LIMIT, STOP_LOSS, STOP_LOSS_LIMIT, STOP_MARKET, TAKE_PROFIT, OCO and CONDITIONAL all rejected with TRADE_PARAMETER_ERROR "invalid type". No fills, no cost. Resolves the open item left by run 1: a protective stop CANNOT be rested on spot via API.
venue_findings.no_perpetuals: CLI capabilities expose market/account/wallet/orders(spot)/bot(futures_grid,spot_grid)/earn(dual) only. There is no plain perpetual order path, so no clean way to express a SHORT. futures_grid is the sole shorting mechanism and is range-bound — wrong instrument for a trending escalation.
venue_findings.size_filters: USOX_USDT basePrecision=3 (size max 3 dp), minAmount=10 USDT, buyCeiling=1.1 / sellFloor=0.9 — limit orders must rest within +/-10% of market. A take-profit further out than +10% cannot be placed.

The best FUNDAMENTAL story found this run: Hormuz LNG transit down 95%, QatarEnergy force majeure since March with 17% capacity offline and 3-5 year repairs, QatarEnergy buying 33 US spot cargoes to serve its own customers, analyst targets raised to $330 (Argus) and $300 (Mizuho). Active war, munitions burn, US strikes on Iran overnight, carrier group rotation, and Gulf air-defence demand after two ballistic missiles hit UAE territory. The view is right: equities are -0.56% into 82% odds of a September hike, an active Middle East war, oil +23% in a month, and a 30y yield at 2007 highs. That is complacency. REJECTED ON STRUCTURE, NOT VIEW - a leveraged short with no stop order type on this venue, held across sessions in which I do not exist, is the precise failure mode CLAUDE.md warns about. If this is ever taken it must be sized so liquidation is unreachable, not sized to the conviction.

Real structural thesis (AI power demand, $90/lb long-term contracts, 173M lb supply vs 204M lb demand). No fresh catalyst today, so no trade; the point of logging it is that the blocker is gone.
